title: Frontend senior systemdesign realtime collab editor
topic: Frontend senior systemdesign realtime collab editor
question: Design the client-side architecture for a real-time collaborative text editor, similar to multiple people editing the same document simultaneously and seeing each other's changes live.
idealAnswer:
The client needs a local, optimistic editing model, a user's own keystrokes must render instantly without waiting for a server round-trip, conflicting edits are reconciled after the fact rather than blocking input

Conflict resolution generally relies on a CRDT (conflict-free replicated data type) or operational transformation, both let concurrent edits from multiple clients converge to the same final state without a central lock, a strong answer explains the core idea of one of these at a high level

A persistent connection (WebSocket or similar) is needed for low-latency bidirectional sync, with a strategy for reconnection and resending unacknowledged local changes if the connection drops

The client needs to render other users' cursors/selections and merge their remote operations into the local document state without disrupting the local user's own in-progress typing or cursor position

Offline or degraded-network handling matters, edits made while disconnected should queue locally and reconcile once reconnected, rather than being lost or blocking the user from typing

Performance at scale matters, for a large document, applying every remote operation individually to the DOM can be expensive, batching updates and using an efficient diffing/rendering strategy is necessary to stay responsive
